studies.title: The magnetic compass
studies.caption: Shen Kuo describes a magnetized needle and notes that it points a little east of true south; by 1119 Zhu Yu reports pilots using it at sea in overcast weather.
studies.prompt: Intimate still-life study in Song China about1088CE of a fine magnetized iron needle suspended horizontally by a nearly invisible silk thread from a small wooden stand; inkstone and brush in background, a scholar watches. No modern compass card or brass pocket compass, no lettering.
